record.question: What is the primary purpose of an oral cholecystogram (OCG)?
options: To assess the function of the liver.
To visualize the gallbladder and assess for the presence of gallstones or other abnormalities.
To image the pancreas and bile ducts simultaneously using an endoscope.
To measure the contractibility of the stomach.
record.explanation: Answer B: To visualize the gallbladder and assess for the presence of gallstones or other abnormalities.. Oral cholecystography was used to image the gallbladder and evaluate gallstones/function; it is now largely replaced by ultrasound. Source/context note: Oral cholecystography is a historical/now rarely used examination; the intended purpose is gallbladder imaging. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/voidcysto; https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/safety-xray. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
